rows.title: Breathe to three

transcript.eng:
Close your eyes. 

Use the magic power of three to stay connected and relax.

Breathe in to the count of three. 1, 2, 3. 
Breathe out to the count of three. 1, 2, 3. 
Breathe in to the count of three. 1, 2, 3. 
Breathe out to the count of three. 1, 2, 3.

Do you feel any different? Deep breathing helps our whole body and mind to calm down. 

You are a star!

text_1_facilitator.eng:
Today’s topic is about what teens see online. As parents, we can feel unsure how to talk about this. 

By staying calm and talking together, you can help your teen feel safe and make good choices online.

rows.text_1_facilitator:
Today’s topic is about what teens see online. As parents, we can feel unsure how to talk about this. 

By staying calm and talking together, you can help your teen feel safe and make good choices online.

text_1_facilitator.eng:
Many teens come across sexual content online, often without looking for it. They may feel curious, confused or uncomfortable. These feelings are normal. 

Talking together helps your teen understand that not everything they see online is real, and learn what respectful, healthy relationships look like.

media_title.eng: Hear how talking openly with her teen helped @data.characters.media_female_1.name talks

media_transcript.eng: The other day, my son told me that a sexual video had popped up on his phone. I didn’t know what to say and I wanted to panic, but instead I listened first and we could talk. It was an uncomfortable conversation, but I'm glad we had it. Now he knows he can come to me if something online worries or confuses him.

Think about:

🙍🏾 **Who made it?** Knowing who created it can help you understand if it is trustworthy.
❓ **Why was it shared?** Some content is made to get attention or to hurt someone — not to show the truth.

text_1_facilitator.eng: Your first response can make a big difference. These four simple steps can help your teen feel safe to keep talking with you.

section_1_title.eng: Stay calm and take a breath

section_1_text.eng: If your teen tells you they have seen something upsetting or sexual online, try to stay calm before you respond. Your first reaction helps your teen decide whether it feels safe to keep talking with you.

section_2_text.eng:
Try asking simple, open questions such as:

“Can you tell me what happened?”
“How did it make you feel?”
“What do you think about what you saw?”
Listen without judging or rushing to solve the problem.

section_3_text.eng:
You could say:
“Thank you for telling me.”
“You did not do anything wrong.”
“We can work through this together.”
This helps reduce shame and makes it more likely your teen will come to you again.

section_4_text.eng: Let your teen know they can always come to you if something online worries or confuses them.

text_1_facilitator.eng: Here are some simple ways you can support your teen when they see or share things online that are confusing or sensitive.

section_1_text.eng:
It’s impossible to protect teens from everything online, but simple routines can reduce exposure. 

Keep devices, including phones, in shared family spaces during the day and at night. Set a good example by following the same rules yourself.

section_1_extra_text.eng:
Set up a central charging spot outside bedrooms. 

Connect with other parents to agree on similar rules - it’s easier for teens to accept rules that their friends’ families also follow.

section_2_text.eng:
Help your teen pause before sharing anything online. Remind them that some videos and pictures are not real or are made to get attention. Ask: Who made this? Why was it shared? Does it feel real? 

If a friend sends a sexual video, it is okay not to pass it on. Your teen can simply say, "I don't send things like that."

section_2_extra_text.eng: Remind your teen that sharing sexual, upsetting or harmful content can hurt both others and themselves. Make sure they know not to share personal information online and to talk to a trusted adult if they are unsure.

section_3_text.eng:
If your teen sees something confusing or sexual online, stay calm and listen. 

Thank them for telling you. 

Reassure your teen that they did nothing wrong. Avoid blame or anger so they feel safe coming to you again.

section_3_extra_text.eng: Keep conversations open, without judging. If upsetting content keeps appearing, discuss simple steps you can take together to help reduce it.

section_4_text.eng:
Teens often learn what relationships look like from what they see online. 

You can help correct that picture. Help your teen understand that real relationships should feel safe, respectful and comfortable for everyone.

section_4_extra_text.eng: Nobody should ever feel pressured to do something they do not want to do.
